I am 60 years old and have worked these 6 mu in Quzhou for 20 years. My wife and I are the only two in the household, so I cannot manage too many scattered plots. Cabbage and Chinese cabbage have always given me stable cash—restaurants and vegetable wholesalers in town come to buy them every year. My well still has water, which is my lifeline for leafy vegetables when the rains fail. I will put 5 mu into my trusted cabbage–Chinese cabbage–cabbage rotation because that is my main income, and I know the timing by heart. I till the soil with a rotary tiller before every crop to break it up fine; heavy ploughing is too slow and hard on my back at this age. For the spring cabbage and autumn cabbage I use improved seeds I have saved and bought from the local supply shop—they are reliable. For summer Chinese cabbage I use hybrid seed because the summer heat brings disease, and the hybrid heads stay tight. Leafy vegetables are hungry, so I give them plenty of nitrogen, but I also put down phosphorus and potassium so the roots hold and the leaves don't yellow. I expect aphids and cabbage worms every year, so I spray pesticides when I see damage; I don't spray blindly, but I don't wait either because one bad week can ruin a whole crop. On the remaining 1 mu I keep 0.5 mu of chili peppers for market money and 0.5 mu of kidney beans for home eating and some side sales. At my age I stick to what this land and my two hands can handle.
